To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD4+ memory T cells expressing PD1, TIGIt and LAG- 3 are enriched in HIV-infeceted cells and contribute to the HIV reservoir during suppressive ART.
CD4+T cells expressing PD- 1, TIGiT, and LAG- 3 are enriched in the HIV latent reservoir in individuals receiving ART and represent a promising target for therapeutic interventions.
CD4+ cells expressing immune checkpoint markers (PD-1,TIGIT, LAG-1) are associated with persistent HIV infection in individuals receiving ART.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapeutic strategies to eradicate HIV from the body.
the development of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of HIV/AIDS.
understanding the immune response in HIV infected people and the mechanisms of viral persistence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PD-1, LAG-2 and TIGIT are associated with HIV persistence in CD4+ T-cells.

CD4 T cell subsets that express immune checkpoint markers such as LAG-3 and PD-1 are enriched for cells carrying HIV genomes and that these cells could be potential targets for immune checkpoint inhibitors.
the expression of immune checkpoint molecules on CD4+ T-cells in HIV-1-infected subjects on ART is associated with the presence of HIV-1 DNA in CD4+ T-cell subsets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PD-1, TIM-3 and LAG-1 are all markers of HIV persistence during ART, and that PD-1 and TIGIT are markers of the inducible HIV reservoir.
PD-1, LAG- 3 and TIGIT co-expression is associated with HIV reservoirs in CD4+ T-cells in individuals on suppressive antiretrovial therapy (ART).
PD-1, LAG- 3 and TIGIT are enriched on cells with inducible HIV DNA and that the frequency of these cells is a predictor for the size of the inducible HIV reservoir.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD4 T cells expressing immune checkpoints are enriched for HIV infected cells during ART.
CD4+T cells expressing PD- 1, TIGiT and LAG- 3 contribute to HIV persistence during ART.
CD4+ memory T cells expressing PD1, TIGT and LAG3 are highly enriched in HIV-inflicted cells in individuals receiving antiretrovial therapy (ART).
